" Ampy is a fork of PlusPlusBattery. 
 Primary target: Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO devices. OnePlus/OPlus devices are also supported as fallback. 
 Upstream: https://github.com/dijia1124/PlusPlusBattery 
 Maintainer: @zenin1504 
 Original author: @dijia1124 aka goodnic 
 Credits: @shminer aka bybycode 
 This app displays the following battery information:
 - Battery Level: The current battery level as a percentage.
 - Status: The current status of the battery (Charging, Discharging, Full, Not Charging).
 - Temperature: The current battery temperature in degrees Celsius.
 - Health: The current health of the battery (Good, Overheat, Dead, Over Voltage, Unknown).
 - Voltage: The current battery voltage in millivolts.
 - Charge Cycle Count: The number of charge cycles the battery has gone through.
 - Battery Current: The instantaneous battery current in milliamperes. Positive while charging, negative otherwise.
 - Battery Design Capacity: The nominal capacity of the battery in milliampere-hours, shown in the Device & Battery card when available.
 - Logcat battery data (experimental): Xiaomi logs are parsed first, with OnePlus/OPlus, Motorola and generic fallbacks. Availability depends on what Android lets the app read.
 "
Please select the entries you want to show in the battery monitor:

For a reliable monitor notification, disable battery optimization (set to "No restrictions") and enable auto-launch for Ampy in system settings. The monitor now keeps refreshing even after you leave or kill the app; Android does not allow any app to restart itself after a forced stop from system settings, so avoid force-stopping Ampy.
Android may prevent apps from using a shorter interval than the system minimum, even when a lower value is selected here.
Setting the refresh interval too low may cause unnecessary battery drain.

Please connect your device to a charger while the battery level is not full (less than 100%)… \nIf data is not showing correctly or nothing shows up, the logcat of your model may have not been supported by Ampy yet, or the logcat does not contain battery related information.

This feature requires a specific BatteryManager API. If the value shows "-1" or "5" all the time, it means it may not be supported on your device. This can happen on Android versions below 14 or, in some cases, on a few devices running Android 14 and even newer.
If this value is less than 10 mV, your device might be reporting battery voltage in V (volt) instead of mV (millivolt), which also leads to an incorrect battery power value.

By default, charge cycles are recorded when the app is opened. You may need to switch between the Dashboard and History tabs to trigger it.\n\nAlternatively, you can enable the \'Automatic daily charge cycle log\' option in Settings for it to be recorded automatically by WorkManager without manually opening the app.
Export all history records to a CSV file? \nEarliest: %1$s\nLatest: %2$s
System values are treated as mA by default. However, some devices report in uA or other units. Please adjust the setting here if your readings appear incorrect.
Allow exact alarms for Ampy so the monitor can be restored after the system kills it while the phone is idle.
